statements.status_notes: Apache HttpComponents Client, when using the classic (blocking) I/O model, fails to release the underlying connection back to the connection manager if the response contains an invalid or unsupported Content-Encoding header value. Repeated requests to a malicious or misbehaving server leak connections and eventually exhaust the connection pool, producing a denial of service. The async I/O model is not affected. Fixed in version 5.6.3.
statements.impact_statement: httpclient5 is already pinned to 5.6.4 (past the 5.6.3 fix), but that alone only holds until a future downgrade, so we also checked reachability of the classic (blocking) client this CVE affects. Two usages exist: a bundled PII-detection filter, which is unreachable - it requires a policy-loading path Liquibase's checks engine never invokes - and the AWS SDK's synchronous Secrets Manager client, which is real but only ever talks to AWS's own TLS-authenticated endpoint. Exploitation needs that server to repeatedly send malformed Content-Encoding responses, so a remote attacker can't trigger this without already controlling or intercepting trusted AWS traffic - the same precondition used for the related Netty HTTP/2 CVEs.
